consent.title: Help us make MakeKeeper better
consent.body: Once a day, this instance can send us a short note saying it is running. Together those notes show how many installs are alive, which plugins people switch on and which versions are still in use — and that is what we go by when we decide what to build next.
consent.saveFailed: Could not save your answer. Please try again.
consent.control: Off by default, and turning it on or off is yours alone: Settings → About → Counting this instance.

instanceId.label: Instance id
instanceId.description: A random identifier this instance made up for itself. Tied to nothing else — not a domain, not an account, not your data.

installMethod.label: Install method
installMethod.description: How this instance was deployed: compose, Coolify, Dokploy, and so on.

plugins.label: Enabled plugins
plugins.description: Which parts of the app are switched on. Identifiers only, never their contents.

locale.label: Language
locale.description: The interface language you work in.

telemetry.frequency: Once a day, while it is switched on. If the instance is off or offline, nothing is queued and nothing is sent later.
telemetry.limits: Nothing else leaves this instance: no project or item names, no files, no accounts, no counts of your data. We store no IP addresses — though Cloudflare, which fronts the receiver, necessarily sees them in transit. The instance id is random and tied to nothing, but it does link this instance's reports to each other, which is what makes counting possible at all.
telemetry.pendingId: Created when you turn this on — there is none yet.
